ai.title: Replace analytics with logger.info in token-count API
ai.summary: Token-count endpoint swaps `trackEvent` calls for `logger.info`. Success logs capture `messageCount`, `hasSystem`, `model`, and `tokenCount`. Error path `trackEvent` removed. Scope limited to `web/src/app/api/v1/token-count/_post.ts`.

eli5.text: The token-counting tool now records its activity in the server's internal log instead of sending events to the analytics system, so you will not see usage data appear in dashboards or reporting tools that previously tracked who called the endpoint. If you look at the server logs, you'll notice each request now writes a line with the number of messages, whether a system prompt was included, the model used, and the token count, replacing the old analytics tracking that recorded the same information in a different system. The error path no longer sends a tracking event at all, so failures are now only visible in the logs rather than in analytics reports.

ai.summary: Refactor `message-block.tsx` to wrap content and attachments in a flex container with gap, removing hardcoded `marginTop`. Update `user-content-copy.tsx` to return null if no content, preventing empty text nodes. Remove `showClipboardMessage` call in `pending-attachments.ts` to reduce noise.

eli5.text: When you send a message that contains only an attachment (like a photo) with no text, the extra blank space that used to appear below it is now gone. The message layout was restructured so content and attachments share a single flexible container with consistent spacing, and attachment-only messages no longer leave an empty text area. Additionally, the brief confirmation that used to pop up when adding an image is no longer shown, reducing visual clutter. These improvements are live today in the CLI.

ai.summary: The codebuff release artifact version advanced from 1.0.601 to 1.0.602 in cli/release/package.json, packaging the prior day's grant-priority reordering, CLI image-attachment race fixes, and context-pruner image preservation work. This is a metadata-only release-bump commit with no source or configuration diffs beyond the version string.
ai.evidence: Commit c4586404 modifies cli/release/package.json, raising the codebuff version field from 1.0.601 to 1.0.602 as a one-line release bump with no other file changes.

eli5.text: Version 1.0.602 improves image handling and credit management for Freebuff users. Images you attach in conversations now load more reliably, with fixes that prevent race conditions and ensure image paths work correctly across directories. The context pruner now keeps images from your most recent message during summarization, so visual details aren't lost when conversations get trimmed. Referral credits now apply before ad credits when you use Freebuff, helping one-time bonuses get used first. The web build process also gained better error logging to catch issues faster during deployment. Upgrading means fewer image glitches and more predictable credit usage.

ai.summary: Added typed mock factories and consolidated testing utilities in `common/src/testing`. Replaces `as any` casts with type-safe mocks for analytics, database, crypto, and streams. New `TESTING_PATTERNS.md` documents best practices for mock cleanup and assertion robustness. Covers `common` package exports and refactors `agent-runtime` fixtures.

eli5.text: The testing tools the team uses to check their software now have a set of pre-made, type-safe mock objects that replace fake copies of analytics, database, crypto, and stream services, so test writers no longer need to use unsafe type casts. A new guide, TESTING_PATTERNS.md, documents the preferred patterns, including always restoring mocks after each test instead of after all tests to prevent state from leaking between tests. These utilities and fixtures are already in the common/src/testing module and are available for any test suite importing from @codebuff/common/testing today.

ai.title: Add diagnostic logging to Discord bot advisory lock
ai.summary: Added structured diagnostic logging to `packages/internal/src/db/advisory-lock.ts` and `web/scripts/discord/index.ts`. New `logLock` and `log` helpers inject timestamps, PIDs, and hostnames into console output to trace lock acquisition, health checks, and shutdown sequences. This change targets production debugging of race conditions or connection drops in the Discord bot's advisory lock mechanism.

eli5.text: When the Discord bot tries to grab or release its exclusive lock on a shared resource, it now writes a detailed note to its logs with a timestamp, the bot's process ID, and (in the bot's own code) the machine's name. This only affects people who read those server-side logs, say, when investigating why the bot lost its lock during a connection drop, so nothing changes for Discord users chatting with the bot. If you were watching the logs, you'd see these new labeled lines appearing at lock-acquisition attempts, every health check, and during shutdown.

ai.title: code-search test fixes
ai.summary: Updated output size limit and timeout handling tests in `sdk/src/__tests__/code-search.test.ts`. Output limit test now verifies truncation via match count and message presence rather than early stop behavior. Timeout test mocks a hung process to ensure `errorMessage` is set without manual close event emission.

eli5.text: If you use the code-search feature, you may have seen confusing failures in the automated checks that guard every software release. Those checks have been rewritten so they no longer depend on fragile details of how the search stops or how a hung search is closed off. Nothing about how code-search works for you has changed today. The new checks simply pass or fail based on whether results are properly truncated and whether timeouts produce a clear error, so future changes to the search code will be validated more reliably.
